h: Rebuke That Makes Divine Presence Tangible

p: "What does 'These are the words' come to teach?
It teaches that they were words of rebuke,
that they were words of rebuke,
you cows of the Bashan,' etc.
what does 'these are the words' come to teach?
That they were words of rebuke, etc.
'And these are the last words of David'
it teaches that they are words of rebuke," etc.
Now the pasuk "These are the words"
from the beginning of the book
and refers to the whole book;
from the pasuk "And Yeshurun grew fat,"
But the purpose of words of rebuke
fear of Hashem in the heart,
that the King of kings of kings,
and immediately fear will come to him
(as is written in the Haggahah at the beginning of Orach Chaim).
And this is what is said (Mishlei 28:23):
"He who rebukes a man after Me
וּבְמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, דְּבָרִים רַבָּה א, ב)
and in the Midrash Rabbah (on this parshah, Devarim Rabbah 1:2):
in order to bring them after Me."
That is, that he should always picture
that Hashem Yisbarach stands before him,
and he should go after Him.
one comes to teshuvah for the past.
the word "fear" is expounded as teshuvah,
אַשְׁרֵי אִישׁ יָרֵא אֶת ה׳ (תְּהִלִּים קיב, א)
"'Fortunate is the man who fears Hashem' (Tehillim 112:1)
fortunate is he who does teshuvah
רֵאשִׁית חָכְמָה יִרְאַת ה׳ (תְּהִלִּים קיא, י)
"'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem' (Tehillim 111:10)
the purpose of wisdom is teshuvah," etc.
And this is indicated by "These are the words,"
which is like "This is the word"
that it is clearly before his eyes,
so that he says of it "this,"
as if pointing with a finger;
and so too "these are the words."
וְזֶה הָיָה כֹּחַ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ בְּיִחוּד
And this was the special power of Moshe Rabbeinu,
that he prophesied with "This is the word"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב סִפְרֵי מַטּוֹת, סִפְרֵי בְּמִדְבַּר קנג)
(as is written in the Sifrei on Matos, Sifrei Bamidbar 153).
And it brings proof from Amos,
that the King of kings of kings stands over him.
"He who rebukes a man after Me"
"in order to bring them after Me,"
לִהְיוֹת אַחֲרֵי ה׳ אֱלֹהֵיכֶם תֵּלֵכוּ (דְּבָרִים יג, ה)
to fulfill "After Hashem your God you shall walk" (Devarim 13:5),
so that the King of kings of kings,
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כג, א)
And likewise what is said (Shmuel II 23:1):
"And these are the last words of David," etc.
so that one points with a finger.
And it is written of David:
"the saying of the man raised on high,"
that he raised up the yoke of teshuvah;
'The words of Koheles, son of David,'" etc.,
even though there is not mentioned there
who was a chariot for the middah of Malchus,
הָיָה גַּם כֵּן כְּמוֹ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
for whom it was clear as if pointed to with a finger,
that the King of kings of kings stands over him,
and he always stands before the King.
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא, ב)
And so it is stated in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 21b):
"Among the prophets none arose like Moshe;
among the kings one did arise";
like "He who rebukes a man after Me,"
to fulfill "After Hashem you shall walk,"
so that the King of kings of kings
(קֹהֶלֶת א, ב; קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה א, ב)
correspond to the six days of work;
and on Shabbos, which he saw — for it is written
that a person sins on it, etc.;
and there can be "those who desecrate it"
the day that is entirely Shabbos.
And the end of his words (Koheles 12:13):
"The end of the matter, all having been heard"
that in the end there will be heard
And for this reason he counted
the words of Koheles as well
And this is what is expounded in the Midrash
(מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, דְּבָרִים רַבָּה א, ב)
(Midrash Rabbah on this parshah, Devarim Rabbah 1:2):
"'Than one who flatters with the tongue'
"one who knows the knowledge of the Most High" (Bamidbar 24:16),
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קצד, א)
and so it is expounded there:
"But among the nations of the world one did arise,
for the Shechinah was speaking from his mouth;
as is written in the holy Zohar
for when you open your mouth
she will speak the words," etc.
that they counted him among the seven
who have no share in the World to Come
And we said that the number seven
for they reasoned that since he
was a chariot for the middah of Malchus
and a blemish was written about him,
וְאַחַר שֶׁיָּצָא הַבַּת קוֹל (אִיּוֹב לד, לג)
And after the Heavenly voice went forth (Iyov 34:33):
"Shall it be repaid according to your mind?" etc.,
corresponding to the middah of Shlomo in holiness
And this is why it is expounded
"than one who flatters with the tongue" about Bilam,
And Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
"'It is good to give thanks — lehodos — to Hashem' (Tehillim 92:2)
For so indicates the middah of Malchus,
which is called "zos," "this," as is known,
that it is clear before his eyes,
that the King of kings of kings stands over him,
and immediately fear comes to him;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א ה, ב)
and through this he comes to teshuvah,
And this is what it says in the Gemara (Tamid 28a):
"As long as there is rebuke in the world,
goodness and blessing come to the world."
that is in it, on Shabbos,
as is written in Sefer HaBahir:
and placed it for them in its place";
And this is what is said: "He who rebukes a man after Me,"
which indicates the holiness of Shabbos,
that the King of kings of kings stands over him.
if only you would find favor before Me
just as you have found favor before Me
all of Creation found favor in His eyes.
And immediately at the entry of Shabbos
and behold, it was very good";
as referring to everything that is the opposite
that from this there will be "very good,"
